mission_03: Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) is a loss function that enables training sequence-to-sequence models without requiring aligned input-output pairs, solving the fundamental problem of mapping variable-length audio sequences to variable-length text transcriptions. The key innovation is introducing a blank token that allows the model to output nothing at certain time steps, and a repeat rule that allows consecutive identical non-blank tokens to represent a single output character. The CTC forward algorithm computes the total probability of all valid alignments between the input sequence and target label sequence using dynamic programming in log space to avoid numerical underflow. The expanded label sequence interleaves blanks between target tokens, and the recursion allows transitions from the same state, the previous state, or skipping over a blank (when the repeat rule permits). CTC loss is the negative log of the sum of probabilities over all valid alignments. Decoding can be done greedily by taking the most likely label at each time step and collapsing repeats, or more accurately using beam search that maintains the top-k most probable partial sequences. In this mission, you will implement the CTC forward algorithm, loss computation, greedy decoding, and beam search decoding.
